brief.situation: 13:00 in a skilled nursing facility. You are the wound management physical therapist. Mr. Ortega, 72, has a sacral pressure injury and a left lateral ankle wound. The standing order says 'hydrocolloid to all wounds, change every 5 days'.
handover: He has diabetes, mild anemia and eats about half his meals. Staff turn him every 2 hours by the clock.
Facility policy: the wound team recommends dressings to match each wound and calls the provider the same day for signs of infection.
howItWorks: The clock runs in simulated time; study pace runs three simulated minutes per real minute. Pause any time.
Each check takes the time on its button. Decide what the findings mean, what to stop or start, and who must know.
Partway through you are asked to write your reasoning. A debrief scores what you did.

scoring.modelReasoning: Select dressings to match wound characteristics and moisture balance. A clean, moist, non-infected stage 2 pressure injury suits a silicone foam dressing, with repositioning planned around the person's risk factors (malnutrition, anemia, age, cognition, sensation) rather than a fixed schedule. A wound with purulence, odor, spreading erythema and fever is infected: do not seal it under an occlusive dressing; get same-day medical assessment.
